title: Design and Implementation of a Custom Hardware Accelerator for SZx Compression in Chipyard
problem: Data movement is a dominant bottleneck in modern computing. Scientific detectors generate unprecedented data volumes (X-ray terabytes/sec, HEP petabytes/sec). Streaming compression with hardware acceleration can reduce data movement overhead.
motivation: Hardware accelerators can improve compression throughput. But hardware compressor evaluation at system level is largely unexplored. Chipyard enables prototyping hardware designs to evaluate system-level performance.
method: Design and implement custom hardware accelerator for SZx (streaming compression) using modern HDLs in Chipyard. Multi-stage state machine, parallel element processing, optimized data transfers. Compare with software baseline.
key_novelty: First hardware accelerator for SZx compression; system-level evaluation framework in Chipyard; hardware-software comparison for compression.
contributions: Custom hardware accelerator for SZx scientific data compression
Multi-stage state machine design for streaming compression
End-to-end system integration on CPU platform
limitations: Early/preliminary study; evaluation in simulation (Chipyard) not silicon; unclear real-world data movement reduction; single workload (SZx); applicability to other compression algorithms unclear.
